ports._goosed_doc: goosed = goose agent ACP/REST+SSE server (goose serve, X-Secret-Key auth, WireGuard-only)

url_health._comment: cloud-url-health-report runtime config. Passwords NEVER live here — NOREPLY_PASSWORD + ME_PASSWORD come from env (sops-decrypted upstream).

concurrency._comment: Private concurrency intentionally low: 16 simultaneous WG probes saturate idle handshakes and cause cascading timeouts on the spokes. 4 is high-enough for the 86 private targets to finish in <30s while staying under the WG renegotiation pressure point.

timeouts._comment: Bumped 2026-05-07: WG re-handshake on idle peers can take ~3-5s before first packet, so a 3s TCP / 5s HTTP-total budget produced false negatives across the 10.0.0.6 spoke (oci-apps) when probing from desktop. New budget allows one full handshake + actual request.

targets._comment: Ports that are not HTTP servers — probe via TcpStream::connect only, skip HTTP GET.

jmap._comment: WG-direct to Stalwart on oci-mail (10.0.0.3:2443) — same transport as the IMAP leg. The public jmap.diegonmarcos.com edge is unreachable/slow from the CI runner.

workflows._comment: Declarative config for the workflow-status audit in reports. Fire rule 3: no hardcoded repo/host names in engine code. Consumed by cloud-health-full-daily (GHA + Dagu fetchers). Evidence goes to reports-logs/dist/workflows/.

checks.description: Only failures within `window_hours` appear in report
Code does not hardcode any of the repos from this JSON

repo_scan._comment: cloud-sec-data-report::repo_scan config. Zero VM CPU — laptop-local. `~/git/cloud-vault/` NEVER scanned: intentional secrets store.
repo_scan._activation_script_patterns_re_comment: Filename patterns identifying ACTIVATION / PROVISIONING scripts. Any content-pattern match inside these files is auto-elevated to CRITICAL — fire rule 3: scripts MUST be data-driven. Anything with a hardcoded password/token/key is P0.

sec_scan._comment: cloud-sec-data-report runtime config. docker_cp_fallback OFF — never load CPU on slow VMs.

runtime_allowlist._comment: Data-driven allowlist for sec-data's runtime container-capability checks (runtime.rs). Every entry is a narrowly-scoped exception -- (vm, container, category) -- for a capability that is genuinely required and already minimized (e.g. cap_add:[SYS_ADMIN] instead of privileged:true). Anything NOT listed here still reports at its normal severity. Downgrades to Info, never silently dropped, so a future accidental widening (e.g. someone adding privileged:true) is still caught.

entries.reason: rclone mount --allow-other needs cap_add:SYS_ADMIN for the FUSE mount() syscall (fusermount3 is a setuid-root helper); privileged:true was removed 2026-07-03 in favor of this narrower grant -- see a_solutions/user-media_photoprism/src/compose.nix.

resolvers._comment: R2: DNS resolvers used by the reports engine, data-driven so they are never hardcoded in checks.rs. `hickory` is the WireGuard-internal DNS hub (gcp-proxy). `public`/`google` are internet anycast constants used to cross-check public resolution — kept here so an operator can repoint them (e.g. to Quad9) without a Rust rebuild. Ports default to 53. reports-common/checks.rs reads this via build-reports.json:.resolvers.

hickory._comment: Internal WG DNS (Hickory) hub. `vm` names the consolidated VM whose wg_ip is the resolver address — resolved at runtime so an IP change in topology propagates automatically. `ip` is a static fallback used only if the consolidated lookup fails.

public._comment: Cloudflare public anycast — internet constant, repointable here.

google._comment: Google public anycast — internet constant, repointable here.

tiers._comment: Phase 1: tiered scan cadence + check-list, data-driven. reports-common Tier enum + --tier CLI flag read this via build-reports.json:.tiers. `interval_secs` is the target cadence; `max_age_secs` is the staleness budget the renderer uses to mark a report STALE (R1) — usually a small multiple of the interval to tolerate one missed run. `checks[]` names the check groups a tier runs; the crate maps names to collectors. Cheaper tiers run more often; deeper tiers run rarely and only off the 1GB VMs.

t0._comment: Heartbeat — island liveness only. Cheapest: 1 TCP + 1 UDP per host. On-VM (health-agent), pushed to health_mesh.

t1._comment: Probe — public surface. No SSH. Runs on edge / GHA.

t2._comment: Deep — SSH into VMs for host/container metrics. GHA over WG.

t3._comment: Forensic — heavy log-mining + audits + scanners. Daily. GHA / oci-apps builder only, NEVER on 1GB VMs.

pipeline.description: Two-stage build: consolidator merges all build.json + config.json sources into the master file; derive emits per-container + archived split files from the master.
source_inputs: vault/secrets.yaml (sops-encrypted secrets per service, key names extracted)

outputs.per_container: 1_cloud-configs/dist/build-{container_or_service_name}.json (one per container, plus one per container-less service — derive output)
outputs.archived: 1_cloud-configs/dist/z_archive/cloud-data-{slice}.json (deprecated split files — kept for soft-transition fallbacks; consumers should read consolidated instead)
